title: Week 32 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “fiscal policy”?
options: Ability to produce more output with the same resources.
Government decisions about spending, taxation, and borrowing that influence the economy.
A rule concerning reserves relative to deposits; requirements have changed over time and may be set at zero.
An institution connecting savers, borrowers, investors, and payment users.
questions.explanation: Fiscal policy means government decisions about spending, taxation, and borrowing that influence the economy.
choices: Ability to produce more output with the same resources.
Government decisions about spending, taxation, and borrowing that influence the economy.
A rule concerning reserves relative to deposits; requirements have changed over time and may be set at zero.
An institution connecting savers, borrowers, investors, and payment users.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “automatic stabilizer”?
options: A tax or spending feature that changes automatically with economic conditions, such as unemployment benefits.
The process by which agencies create regulations under statutory authority.
A model with many firms, identical products, easy entry, and price-taking behavior.
The process through which people develop political values, identities, and habits.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “multiplier”?
options: The total change in output associated with an initial change in spending or taxation under specified conditions.
An argument about what government should do, based on goals, evidence, feasibility, and tradeoffs.
The quantities producers are willing and able to sell at different prices during a stated period.
Recurring expansions and contractions in aggregate economic activity.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “crowding out”?
options: The agreement creating proportional representation in the House and equal state representation in the Senate.
The difference between willingness to pay and the price actually paid.
Reduced private investment or activity associated with government borrowing or resource use.
Output per unit of labor or other input.
questions.explanation: Crowding out means reduced private investment or activity associated with government borrowing or resource use.
choices: The agreement creating proportional representation in the House and equal state representation in the Senate.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “national debt”?
options: A sustained rise in the general price level, reducing money’s purchasing power.
The rate charged on eligible borrowing from Federal Reserve lending facilities.
The accumulated outstanding federal borrowing resulting from past deficits and other financing operations.
A representative government limited by a constitution and accountable to the people and law.
questions.explanation: National debt means the accumulated outstanding federal borrowing resulting from past deficits and other financing operations.
choices: A sustained rise in the general price level, reducing money’s purchasing power.
The rate charged on eligible borrowing from Federal Reserve lending facilities.
The accumulated outstanding federal borrowing resulting from past deficits and other financing operations.
A representative government limited by a constitution and accountable to the people and law.

options: Interest and principal payments associated with public debt.
The election in which voters choose among nominees and decide public offices or measures.
A tax intended to align private incentives with an external social cost.
The value of the best alternative forgone when a choice is made.
questions.explanation: Debt service means interest and principal payments associated with public debt.

questions.question: Which action best demonstrates mastery of the Week 32 inquiry?
options: A student accepts the first available claim or offer without checking the source, terms, evidence, or consequences.
A student distinguishes deficit from debt and conditions any multiplier or crowding-out claim on the state of the economy and policy design.
A student relies on political identity, advertising, or personal preference as a substitute for documented analysis.
A student selects an answer only because it sounds confident, even when the record is incomplete or contradictory.
